text: You've been playing for hours, hooked on progress. That next level, that big achievement, feels incredibly close, almost within reach.
You dive into the next challenge, expecting victory, ready for that progress bar to finally fill. This is the moment you’ve worked towards.
Suddenly, everything changes. Enemies get tougher, puzzles more complex. Every attempt ends in frustrating failure. The game feels actively against you.
That's because it often is. Designers use dynamic difficulty scaling and 'engagement loops' to keep you on the edge, but still playing.
The game isn't for quick wins. It's designed to keep you invested, chasing that elusive finish line, encouraging more time or in-app purchases.
So, next time a game feels unfairly hard, remember: it’s not just you. It’s an invisible system, crafted to maximize playtime and keep you coming back.
